title: Human Performance
authority: Fitts was a pioneer of engineering psychology and Air Force human-factors research; Posner a leading cognitive psychologist. The book is the standard source for the cognitive, associative and autonomous stages of skill learning.
caveats: A short, now classic textbook; the three stages are a descriptive framework with fuzzy boundaries, not discrete measured phases. Stage boundaries vary by task. DOI, issue and page range removed because they could not be confirmed this session (web search budget exhausted); title, authors, journal and year are from memory and should be checked.

title: Studies on the telegraphic language: The acquisition of a hierarchy of habits
authority: Bryan and Harter produced the first systematic learning-curve study of a real-world skill (telegraphy) and are credited with the concept of the learning plateau and of hierarchical habits.
caveats: Plateau interpretation later challenged (Keller 1958, 'The phantom plateau'); plateaus appear in some data sets and not in others, and can be artifacts of averaging or changes in strategy or motivation. DOI should be rechecked. DOI, issue and page range removed because they could not be confirmed this session (web search budget exhausted); title, authors, journal and year are from memory and should be checked.

title: The role of deliberate practice in the acquisition of expert performance
authority: Ericsson was the leading researcher on expertise; the paper defined deliberate practice and is among the most cited in the field.
caveats: Practice hours were retrospective self-estimates from small samples (violinists, pianists). Macnamara et al. 2014 meta-analysis found deliberate practice explains much less variance than claimed; Macnamara and Maitra 2019 replication found weaker group differences. Definition disputes (teacher-designed or not).

title: Deliberate practice and performance in music, games, sports, education, and professions: A meta-analysis
authority: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis in a leading psychology journal; the main empirical counterweight to the 10,000-hour narrative.
caveats: Ericsson and Harwell (2019) argue the inclusion criteria were too broad (included non-deliberate practice and retrospective hours). Variance figures should be checked against the original table before quoting.

title: A schema theory of discrete motor skill learning
authority: Schmidt is a founding figure of motor learning research and co-author of the standard textbook Motor Control and Learning.
caveats: The variability-of-practice prediction is well supported in children and mixed in adults. Schema theory is about discrete, brief movements; extension to continuous tasks like flying is by analogy. DOI, issue and page range removed because they could not be confirmed this session (web search budget exhausted); title, authors, journal and year are from memory and should be checked.

title: Knowledge of results and motor learning: A review and critical reappraisal
authority: Highly cited review in a top review journal that reinterpreted the knowledge-of-results literature and proposed the guidance hypothesis.
caveats: Later work (Wulf and Shea 2002) found that for complex skills and novices more frequent feedback early can help; the guidance hypothesis is best supported for simple tasks.

title: New conceptualizations of practice: Common principles in three paradigms suggest new concepts for training
authority: Two leading researchers (motor learning and memory) synthesizing three research traditions into a training principle.
caveats: Benefits of difficulty depend on learner readiness (Guadagnoli and Lee 2004 challenge point). Learners and instructors misjudge learning by in-practice performance. DOI, issue and page range removed because they could not be confirmed this session (web search budget exhausted); title, authors, journal and year are from memory and should be checked.

title: Contextual interference effects on the acquisition, retention, and transfer of a motor skill
container: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Learning and Memory
authority: The founding experiment of the contextual interference effect, in a top experimental psychology journal.
caveats: Effect is robust in laboratory tasks but weaker or absent in some applied tasks, with children, and with very complex skills; novices may be overloaded by fully random practice. DOI, issue and page range removed because they could not be confirmed this session (web search budget exhausted); title, authors, journal and year are from memory and should be checked.

title: Optimizing performance through intrinsic motivation and attention for learning: The OPTIMAL theory of motor learning
authority: Wulf is the leading researcher on attentional focus; the paper is a long theoretical review.
caveats: Authors' own program dominates the evidence base; some replications and moderators remain debated, and the dopamine account is speculative.

title: Incremental transfer effectiveness
authority: Roscoe was a founder of aviation psychology; the paper introduced the transfer effectiveness ratio and its incremental form.
caveats: Ratios depend on how criterion and time are measured and on the instructor; most data are military or airline. Check the DOI. DOI, issue and page range removed because they could not be confirmed this session (web search budget exhausted); title, authors, journal and year are from memory and should be checked.

title: Transfer of landing skills in beginning flight training
authority: Controlled transfer experiment with beginning students at the University of Illinois Institute of Aviation, by leading aviation training researchers.
caveats: Results not retrieved; only the design (beginning Illinois flight students given two simulator landing sessions before aircraft landing practice) was confirmed. Journal, volume and pages confirmed by an SAE citation record. DOI not confirmed.

title: Flight simulator training effectiveness: A meta-analysis
authority: Peer-reviewed meta-analysis by Navy training researchers; the standard citation for simulator training adding to aircraft training.
caveats: Effect sizes not retrieved. Journal, volume, issue and pages confirmed by a citing reference list. Mostly military studies; weak reporting is a known limit of the simulator literature.

title: It is not how much you have but how you use it: Toward a rational use of simulation to support aviation training
authority: Leading training-science researchers; the paper is the canonical argument against equating simulator realism with training value.
caveats: A position paper, not an experiment; I confirmed only the abstract this session.

title: Transfer of skill from a computer game trainer to flight
authority: Gopher is a leading attention researcher; the study used Israeli Air Force flight cadets and real flight scoring.
caveats: Cadets, not civilian beginners; Space Fortress is a purpose-built attention-management trainer, not a commercial game. Does not support general claims that video games improve flying. Journal, volume and pages confirmed by listings.

title: Effectiveness of part-task training and increasing-difficulty training strategies: A meta-analysis approach
authority: Wickens is among the most cited human-factors researchers; a meta-analysis of 37 transfer studies.
caveats: Modest number of studies; moderator analyses are coarse; mixed task types.

title: Do team and individual debriefs enhance performance? A meta-analysis
authority: Meta-analysis of 46 samples (N = 2,136) by two training researchers.
caveats: Most studies are team or medical settings; individual flight debriefing is a small part of the data. Moderators (facilitation, structure) are tentative.

title: Transfer of training effectiveness of personal computer-based aviation training devices
publisher: Federal Aviation Administration, Office of Aerospace Medicine (DOT/FAA/AM-97/11)
authority: Federal aviation research report by the University of Illinois aviation team; the main controlled evidence on PC simulators for instrument training.
caveats: Instrument-rating tasks, not primary flight training or MSFS 2024; PCATD hardware (yoke, rudder, throttle) was required. A 1999 journal version is suggested by a citing source but its citation could not be confirmed, so it is not listed.
